Life Story

The second son of Akitt’s mother’s brother, Lynd has always worked hard and led an active outdoor life. He is extremely fit, looking somewhat younger than his 34 years. His blue eyes are a striking contrast to his jet black hair and make him stand out in a crowd. He is cocky and proud of his body, wearing tight leather pants and a leather jerkin which emphasize his physique. Lynd is a darling with the ladies. Although intelligent, he talks quite slowly, appearing to pause and carefully consider every word. Lynd is definitely more capable than his cousin, but fate granted the manor to Akitt. Lynd stays for the easy money.

Life Story

Noble by birth, with some noble skills (such as literacy), he is essentially a guildsman (timberwright) with delusions of glory. Years of hate and fear have left him gaunt, haggard and looking much older than his twentyseven years of age. He has brown eyes and dark brown hair. Although he tries to project a cheerful demeanour, he is slightly paranoid and cheap with his money. He is well dressed (preferring maroon) but over-accessorized, showing his desperate desire to be accepted as one of the gentle folk. Despite his attempts to fit in, he tends to be shuffled aside in conversations.

Life Story

A broker for the timberwright’s guild, Naviel is a follower. Reasonably intelligent, he hates to make decisions and prefers to defer to others. He is of average size, with a slim build, green eyes and brown hair. He wears good clothes that always seem a little baggy on him as if they were hand-me-downs. Naviel has no tact and bluntly says whatever comes to mind. For the last five years, he has acted as Akitt’s agent, finding buyers for the timber and investing his profits. He has an extensive array of shady and illegal contacts throughout the kingdom. He keeps one penny in seven of Akitt’s ill-gotten gains.

text.content:
The PCs do not have to travel all the way back to Gardiren if the GM doesn’t want them to. Simply presenting the fugitive and the warrant at any of the Earl’s far flung vassal manors can be a short cut to the reward (though the sum will be decreased by the cost of returning the prisoner(s) to Gardiren). GMs can use this device to draw the PCs great distances to the site of the next chapter of his current campaign. If the GM wishes, the Earl can have representatives in any town convenient to the capture of the outlaws (even Thay).

This adventure also introduces the PCs to the dangerous, unpredictable but sometimes lucrative world of bounty hunting. A successful team could earn a letter of recommendation from the Earl and introductions to other nobles with similar “problems”.

History

The Earl’s father was a man of lusty appetites, even in his later years. He fathered several bastards including Akitt Llack. Akitt was acknowledged and lived with his mother in one of the Earl’s townhouses until the Earl died when he was twelve. His father’s widow hated him and ordered him and his mother immediately expelled from the only home he had ever known.

On the death of the Earl’s widow a decade later, Akitt was brought back to court. With his mother dead, Earl Curo wanted to ensure his half-brother was taken care of, be he baseborn or no. However, the life of the timberwright’s apprentice had ill-prepared Akitt for the life at court and he soon made a fool of himself.

Anxious to rid himself of an embarrassment, the Earl made Akitt bailiff of a rich manor on the edge of his domain. Thinking he was being quite magnanimous, Curo sent Akitt off to the wilderness without recognizing the humiliation, rage and hate boiling in his veins.

Details

Akitt arrived at Charmic Manor five years ago. He took over a rich, successful manor which had been well tended by conscientious bailiffs for forty years. Within weeks he began to strip it bare. He sold off valuable equipment and furnishings; he allowed his cousin to illegally cut and sell the King’s timber; and he drove the peasants mercilessly, squeezing every penny out of them while not spending a farthing on manor upkeep. Using a pair of ruthless mercenaries and a few cottar lackeys, he held the villagers prisoner in their own homes. For years, the people prayed for the Earl to visit and see what Akitt had done. The Earl never came.

What the peasants didn’t know was that Akitt made a point of personally delivering his annual feudal payment to Gardiren. He would visit the Earl and enjoy a pleasant dinner and smoothly lie to his half-brother, thanking him for granting him the position of bailiff and explaining how country life had helped him grow up and become more responsible. The Earl’s Steward had no reason to check Akitt, especially since the annual revenues from the manor remained the same as under previous bailiffs.

Finally, Charmic’s Peonian priest could take no more and slipped away in the night to take word to the Earl. After walking all day, the priest arrived at the Earl’s castle in the middle of a feast. He convinced the guard to call the Steward out of the hall and informed him what had happened. When the Steward relayed the news to the Earl he summoned the village priest before him, questioning him in detail. Then the Earl summoned the local Peonian priest from Gardiren to confirm the man was indeed from Charmic. Determined to convince the Earl, the village priest fell to his knees and swore a holy vow on the sacred relic of Peoni. Convinced by the man’s honesty, Earl Curo was furious and declared “the ungrateful wretch” outlaw. The Earl charged him with Abuse of Trust and Larceny and he was tried and found guilty “in absentia.” The Earl’s command to his men was clear, “Bring me Akitt. Alive if possible, dead, just as good.”

As he hurried through the town of Gardiren, the village priest was recognized by one of Akitt’s “business partners”, Naviel, who realized they would all hang when the Earl found out what was happening. Naviel rode to Charmic to warn Akitt while the Earl was busy interrogating the priest. In a flurry of activity, the bailiff, his halfbrother, two mercenary guards and Naviel rode out of Charmic in the middle of the night, only hours ahead of the Earl’s guards.

The manor is now in the temporary guardianship of Sir Peart Tanush, one of the Steward’s assistants, while the hue and cry has gone out for Akitt’s head. Although horses were heard, the villagers were too afraid to watch Akitt leave and no one knows which way he went.

Crucial Rumour

Although the GM may allow the PCs several false starts, the vital piece of information they must uncover in Charmic is that Akitt has most likely fled to Tashal. There are two ways they can find this out.

  1. On one trip, he took one of his lackeys, a cottar (@UUID[JournalEntry.zhwcK5xXatRfQwrv.JournalEntryPage.wrstErZ7IdTOgcNU]{[32] Cottar-Beadle (Kloril of Clan Ibin)}) well known to all the other villagers as Akitt’s lapdog. On his return, the cottar bragged that they were welcomed like kings at the Timberwright’s Guild Hall. Akitt deposited money with several usurers in the city.
  2. As they hurriedly packed, the cook overheard Lynd tell Akitt that they needed to loose themselves in the big city until they could find a caravan out of the realm.

Other Rumours at Charmic Manor

  1. Akitt left the village by the north road. The villein (@UUID[JournalEntry.zhwcK5xXatRfQwrv.JournalEntryPage.xn5csoCgj1USaq8F]{[2] Villein (Eld of Clan Kralis)}) thinks that he has gone to Tashal via the main road through Bidow. GM Note: The villein is correct; they did leave by the north road.
  2. Akitt left the village by the east road. The cottar (@UUID[JournalEntry.zhwcK5xXatRfQwrv.JournalEntryPage.IM0gHuTm4ysE91MC]{[31] Cottar (Arath of Clan Narad)}) believes he has taken the trail east to Naniom Bridge and south through Getha to Kiban. GM Note: This is one of Akitt’s lackeys who is trying to ingratiate himself with the new regime. He didn’t see anything.
  3. One of the mercenaries once boasted to the stable boy about having crossed Naniom Bridge and following the trail south to Nenda and Minarsas, though the boy has no idea where these places are. GM Note: Possible but unlikely. A search of the manor will determine they did not take more than a few days’ provisions with them.
  4. A cottar (@UUID[JournalEntry.zhwcK5xXatRfQwrv.JournalEntryPage.8bRTPB2XJhjkGQYF]{[1] Cottar (Girn of Clan Valada)}) who worked for Lynd thinks they went cross country to Ascur Abbey and then on to Tashal. Lynd seemed to know his way through the woods and often mentioned the abbey was only five leagues away over a couple of ridges. GM Note: A quick search of the road leading south into the forest will make it very obvious that five men on horseback and three mules could not have passed this way.
  5. One of the quarrymen out for a liaison with his sweetheart saw men riding north. He figures they slipped through Gardiren in the night and headed north on Noron’s Way. GM Note: The quarryman did see Akitt and his men, but Akitt is unlikely to have risked heading right though Gardiren. The Earl’s guards would have seen him.

Rumours in Tashal

  1. One of the guards at the Timberwright’s Guild Hall says he probably headed west at Heru and travelled north-west past Olokand on the Fur Road. There are plenty of places to hide in Orbaal. GM Note: The guard is Orbaalese. As far as anyone knows, neither Akitt nor any of his men have ever travelled this way.
  2. Akitt and his men stabled their horses at the Tower Inn across from the Timberwright’s Guild. One of the stable boys remembers they left in the company of several pilgrims headed south along the Genin Trail towards Chybisa. GM Note: This is correct. If asked the stable boy can give a description of their new clothes.
  3. A caravan left for Tharda via the Salt Route the day after Akitt fled Charmic Manor. GM Note: There was not enough time for Akitt to reach Tashal and join this caravan. A few bribes around the Timberwright’s Guild Hall will confirm he was seen here the day after the caravan left.
  4. A group of Khuzan left Tashal yesterday headed west on the Silver Way towards Azadmere. They were accompanied by many men with horses and mules. One particularly wealth man travelled with them. He was accompanied by two servants and two guards. GM Note: If the PCs ask around, someone will be able to tell them, the man was a well known merchant who frequently deals with the Khuzan.

Rumours on the Genin Trail

  1. The sisters at Erune Nunnery hosted the pilgrim group a day or two before (depending on how close the PCs are). They remember the stocky man in maroon clothes and his servant with the shocking blue eyes. GM Note: The sisters are correct, this is the group.
  2. The gate warden thinks the pilgrims will next stop at Wylain Chapterhouse because they have two Meken of the Lady of Paladins with them. GM Note: This is wrong; the pilgrims will make for Ledyne Abbey to pray at the Bishop’s temple.

Option 1: Upon being captured, Akitt bargains for his life, claiming that the majority of his stolen money is buried in three large treasure chests just south of Charmic Manor in the hills. There is no map and only Akitt knows the exact location. He agrees to lead the PCs to the treasure if they let him go alive. There are no treasure chests. The rest of Akitt’s money is in the form of bearer promissory notes sewn into the lining of his leather jerkin. Akitt will try and escape from the PCs en route to Charmic Manor.

Option 2: If Akitt is successful in bargaining for his life, he turns over several bearer promissory notes to the PCs and then flees. When the PCs try and cash the notes, they find out they are poor quality forgeries. Now the PCs are not just hunting a felon, but someone who has cheated them personally. Akitt has made good use of his lead and has already well on his way to Thay. He has cashed one of the real notes and hired four skilled mercenaries at the nearest town. They have two horses each and are riding them hard down the Genin Trail and maybe already in Chybisa already.

Option 3: By the time the PCs catch up to Akitt, he has already been captured by smarter or luckier bounty hunters. Now the PCs are faced with losing their reward or stealing him out from under the competition. The competition consists of a very similar party to the PCs. They have tied Akitt to a tree in the centre of their camp and are taking turns on sentry duty. They plan to head north to Gardiren the morning after the PCs find them. They also bear warrants signed by the Steward of the Earl and killing the opposing bounty hunters could have serious legal ramifications for the PCs.

Simple greed is the easiest motivation. The Earl is offering a substantial reward for the head of his half-brother (a minimum of £5 is suggested, though the GM can scale this to match his campaign). The Earl will pay the party on presentation of Akitt (alive) or his head. Lynd, Naviel and the two mercenaries are worth only a small amount (£1 each) as they are only accessories.

If the PCs are already in the service of the Earl, then they may be dispatched after the traitor. Feudal duty is a simple stick the GM can use to send the PCs on a merry goose chase. The recently vacated position of bailiff of Charmic Manor could be a powerful carrot for one of the Earl’s retinue, especially a poor hedge knight.

If the PCs are not already in the service of the Earl, they may see this as an opportunity to seek his favour. Besides paying a healthy reward, the Earl will look very favourably on a group that can act quickly and decisively on his behalf. As above, if the PC group includes a knight, the Earl might even consider granting the manor to the knight in lieu of a cash reward. A skilful negotiator might even win relief from feudal obligation for a few years while the manor is restored to order. This could lead to a whole new adventure rebuilding the manor, restoring the villagers faith and protecting the manor from wolves (on four legs or two).

Another option open to the GM is revenge. If one of the PCs is from the afflicted village, word of abuse of a loved one may spur them to action. The rape of a mother or sister or the theft of family land is sure to send the PCs after Akitt for revenge with a nice profit thrown in for good measure.

Earl Curo is a corpulent libertine who enjoys the pleasures of his table, but is none the less a competent intriguer. No matter his politics, his dispute with Akitt is personal. He did not want to send his half-brother away when his father died, but his mother insisted and Curo has regretted it ever since. He really felt that he was doing Akitt a favour when he brought him back to his court five years ago, but it soon became apparent that life as a timberwright’s apprentice had ill prepared him for the gossip and intrigue of court life. Curo hoped to spare his halfbrother from torment by setting him up in a very profitable little manor where he could live comfortably, comfortably out of sight. When word reached Earl Curo of the wanton rape and loot of Charmic Manor, he was furious. His anger was genuine and his vengeance swift, but legal. As Lord, he has power of life and death over his subjects and is well within his authority to declare Akitt wolfs head.

The relationship between the PCs and the Earl can vary widely. If they have already worked for the Earl or come with a letter of recommendation, he may commission them directly. If they are strangers, this may be their chance to ingratiate themselves with a powerful new patron. Whatever their relationship, in the matter of Akitt, the Earl will be completely honest and trustworthy.

Warrant

If the PCs think to ask, the Earl’s Steward is willing to draft a warrant deputizing the PCs as agents of the Earl charged with arresting Akitt, Lynd and any accomplices. Although it has the force of law in the Earl’s lands, it may be less valuable outside of his territory. However, it would be helpful in explaining why the PCs have five men tied up and are transporting them back to Gardiren. If the PCs kill Akitt and/or his men, the warrant will offer some protection from a charge of murder, though they may spend a few days in the dungeon until the validity of the warrant can be confirmed.

In addition to making the PCs legal bounty hunters, the warrant can be used to seek hospitality from the manors of the Earl’s vassals. PCs may also enlist the Earl’s vassal’s help in capturing Akitt, though they would expect to share the reward for their trouble. PCs that remain for the rest of the feast will see one or more other groups requesting warrants from the Steward. There is at least one other group actively searching for the fugitives and the game of concealing clues from their opponents can add an additional level of complexity to the chase if the GM wishes to play up this factor.

Beginning at Charmic Manor, Nephshire in the Kingdom of Kaldor, the trail of the reneged bailiff leads to the city of Tashal and from there to the Genin Trail. The GM may use this pursuit to lead PCs towards other adventures or have them end up back where they started.

Alternately, the GM may begin the adventure at any small country manor, leading the PCs to a nearby major town and from there on a merry chase though back roads and down trade routes. The adventure is easily adapted to any manor and any great lord (Earl, Baron or Bishop)

Akitt, accompanied by his cousin Lynd, his two mercenaries and Naviel (his business partner), fled in the middle of the night north to Erathald Manor before turning west cross country past Emyln and Tirachane Manors. The skirted Bidow and were past Urveve Abbey before sun up. The almost killed their horses doing it and were forced to walk their animals though most of the next day.

They spend the following night huddled in a cold camp off the road. The next morning they arrived in Tashal ahead of any news of Akitt’s being declared outlaw. They were warmly welcomed at the Timberwright’s Guild Hall. Akitt spent the day gathering up his ill-gotten wealth from usurers and investments around the city. He converted much of it into promissory notes drawn on Thay usurers, while keeping £8 in silver pennies in an iron bound chest and £2 in gold coins in his waist pouch. Lynd arranged passage out of the city. Naviel purchased new clothes, arranged for fake letters of introduction and purchased additional weapons and armour.

Akitt assumed the identity of Letos, a pious Laranian on his way to Thay to visit the temple of the Primate. He is accompanied by his two servants (Lynd and Naviel) and two bodyguards. The five men joined a group of wealthy pilgrims travelling south on the Genin Trail by horseback. The men have bought additional mules to carry food and provisions for the trip. The pilgrims left the next day (two days after Akitt fled Charmic Manor). They are travelling on the main road. Akitt is quite concerned because he feels they are travelling too slowly, but his cousin Lynd has convinced him that five men travelling quickly with heavily laden pack mules would attract even more attention. Naviel has also urged caution because he fears travelling the Genin Trail without a large party for protection.

The distance Akitt and his men have managed to travel is up to the GM. Also, if the GM wishes, they can have departed on one of the other routes suggested in the rumours above. Lightly burdened PCs should be able to catch up with the group even if they are travelling on foot, because although the wealthy members of the pilgrim party are on horseback, most of their servants are on foot. The pilgrims only travel one watch per day.

The pilgrim group totals twenty-three, including Akitt and his men, a knight from Balimshire (with his wife and six servants), a Laranian priest from Abriel (with two lay brothers), two Meken (common soldiers) of the Order of the Lady of Paladins (travelling with the group as far as Nebulan Chapter House) and a merchant (with four servants and a wagon) who has also joined the group for protection. The GM may wish to develop this group further if they are involved in the capture of Akitt by the PCs. Although very vague about his past and where he comes from, Akitt has turned on all his charm and ingratiated himself with the group. Unless convinced otherwise, the other pilgrims will help protect Akitt from attack.

Rationale

Akitt Llack began life in the comfortable world of privilege. The son (abet bastard) of the Earl, he had the best clothes, best food and a house he shared with his mother close to the castle. He learned to read and write and expected to become a page. With his father’s death, he and his mother became persona non gratis, especially with his father’s widow who hated his mother and saw Akitt as the embodiment of the infidelity of her husband. They were thrown out of their house in the middle of the night, stripped of everything but the underwear they were wearing. In shock, they were forced to beg for shelter from Akitt’s grandfather who had disowned his daughter years before for her wanton ways.

Akitt spent the next decade as little more than a serf. He was beaten and worked mercilessly by his grandfather, a timberwright, and then forced to watch his mother beg his grandfather not to throw them out ever time he got drunk. Akitt grew up a bitter and hateful young man.

Motives and Goals

When the Earl invited Akitt back to court, the young man saw it as his opportunity to get revenge on the nobles who ruined his life and taken the money he felt he was owed. Unfortunately, his lack of martial training or courtly graces quickly made him the butt of every joke in the Earl’s court, making him even angrier. When his half-brother offered him the position of bailiff of some godforsaken dung-heap in the country, he took it, feigning gratitude with the full intention of raping it for every penny he could before leaving Kaldor forever.

The manor is now in the temporary guardianship of Sir Peart Tanush, one of the Steward’s assistants, while the hue and cry has gone out for Akitt’s head. Although horses were heard, the villagers were too afraid to watch Akitt leave and no one knows which way he went.

Akitt’s succeeded in stealing a large sum from the Earl (and King, in the form of timber). He plans to escape from Kaldor and make his way to another kingdom. There, he will buy himself a townhouse and live the life of luxury he feels he has earned.

Recent activities

Every few months, accompanied by Naviel, representatives of the timberwright’s guild would visit to buy timber. In the last two months, Akitt has made several trips to Tashal. Akitt avoided Gardiren except for his annual feudal payment to his half-brother.

Relationships

Akitt’s mother and grandfather are both dead. His only living family is an uncle, aunt and two cousins. One of the cousins, Lynd, has been living with him since he took over the manor and has forced the villagers to build him a large house and outbuildings in the centre of the village. Lynd and Akitt are thick as thieves, constantly plotting together. The villager’s believe Akitt’s uncle is also a timberwright and part of the scam. They have no idea where he lives, but he is not in Gardiren.

Akitt has two mercenaries who have served him for the last five years. They are completely amoral bullies who will obey Akitt as long as he pays them. For mercenaries, they are relatively trustworthy and loyal, meaning they won’t murder him in his sleep, but they will not die for him and if the odds are against them they will flee, taking whatever they can get their hands on.

Guildsmen

Akitt grandfather died after he was made bailiff of Charmic. A journeyman timberwright, Akitt assumed his grandfather’s position as a master; he was definitely not qualified, but well placed bribes ensured he was confirmed. He bears the credentials of a master timberwright and as such has access to the guild’s extensive network of guild halls and members. Lynd is a journeyman though he is actually more skilled than Akitt. If he has reason to suspect an attack, Akitt is not afraid to make up a story and seek the assistance of his fellow guildsmen. Since they often work deep in the forest, timberwrights arm themselves, their journeymen and apprentices.

The timing of the pursuit is vital to the PCs being able to catch Akitt and his men. It is up to the GM to adjust the pace to ensure he is not caught too quickly but also to keep the excitement up and not let the pursuit to drag out and last too long.

The most logical action upon accepting the mission is for the PCs to go to Charmic. That is where Akitt was last seen and the manor may hold clues to where he has gone. Unless the PCs race to the manor down unfamiliar roads in the middle of the night (a bad idea), the Earl’s guards will arrive before them (they will depart at first light). The PCs can search the manor and interview all potential witnesses in about a day. Their next destination will depend on what they uncover. This is also an opportunity for the GM to introduce the possibility that a grateful Earl might be looking for a new bailiff to install at Charmic Manor.

Upon accepting the mission, the PCs might decide to act immediately and head down the Tashal road rather than checking out the manor as suggested above. In that event, it is suggested that the PCs be allowed to pass Akitt and his men camped out in the woods along side the road. Then, rather than openly entering the city, Akitt, Lynd and Naveil will enter the city separately in disguise to complete their various tasks (listed under The Truth below). This can lead to a cat and mouse game through the streets of Tashal. The two mercenaries wait with the horses and mules outside the city. The GM may allow the PCs to catch Lynd or Naviel in order to ratchet up the tension.

If the PCs are slow to act or spend too much time chasing down false leads at Charmic Manor, it is suggested that Akitt have problems collecting his money or finding a group travelling the direction he wants to go. This should result in additional rumours and clues being left as Lynd searches the inns for people travelling south. Barkeeps and innkeepers will remember this distinctive man, thus speeding up the process of the PCs discovering the bailiff and his men have left on the Genin Trail. A broken wagon wheel could also delay the pilgrims.

Finally, the location the PCs catch up with the fugitives depends on where the GM wants to stage the final confrontation. Eliten Manor has already been mapped and is on the route and may be easier for a rushed GM rather than having to map Erone Nunnery, Wylain Chapter House or Ledyne Abbey. Alternately, a final confrontation staged in or near Tashal might be more enjoyable for a group of urban adventurers.

Difficulty: Low to Moderate

The Bastard Baliff is a "Adventure Module"; it describes an adventure starting in Norther Kaldor (Gardiren and Charmic Manor), then proceeding south to Tashal and possibly down the Genin trail to Thay.

This mini-adventure is suitable for use in any campaign as a fill-in between larger adventures, a side-track to generate some quick money or as an introduction to the service of Earl Curo of Gardiren. It is set in Kaldor, but can be easily adapted to suit any campaign location. It may be played at any time of the year.

This module is based on the "The Bastard Bailiff" fanon; please see @UUID[JournalEntry.HD0hlurPhyfLRJQX.JournalEntryPage.WVIv1Lqgiv95fDbj]{Credits} for more information.

 

Using this module with Non-HârnMaster systems

This module, with the exception of the Actors, is system-agnostic.  See the section below on NPCs for details about the villans who are provided as HârnMaster 3 Actors; these details may be used to generate appropriate statistics for your game system.

 

Lead-Ins

Liegemen: Word arrives from Earl Curo that his bastard, half-brother Akitt Llack is declared outlaw and all loyal liegemen are to be on the lookout for him.

Bounty Hunters: The town crier reads news that Earl Curo has offered a reward for any man who will bring him Akitt Llack, dead or alive.

Dinner Guests: A fortunate encounter results in an invitation to dinner at Earl Curo’s hall. During dinner, a messenger arrives. Upon hearing of his bastard halfbrother’s betrayal, the Earl offers a bounty to any man who will track down the rogue who has betrayed him.

 

Setting

Beginning at Charmic Manor, Nephshire in the Kingdom of Kaldor, the trail of the reneged bailiff leads to the city of Tashal and from there to the Genin Trail. The GM may use this pursuit to lead PCs towards other adventures or have them end up back where they started.

Alternately, the GM may begin the adventure at any small country manor, leading the PCs to a nearby major town and from there on a merry chase though back roads and down trade routes. The adventure is easily adapted to any manor and any great lord (Earl, Baron or Bishop).

 

Objective

The object of this adventure is quite straightforward, pursuit Akitt with all possible speed, following a chain of rumours and clues until he is caught. Once the PCs find Akitt they must decide what they are going to do. If they kill him, they need to take proof (preferably his head) back to the Earl. If they capture him, it could be a whole new adventure getting him back to Gardiren.

If captured, Akitt will try and buy his freedom. It is up to the GM how much money he has skimmed from Charmic over the last five years. He has also been brokering timber and investing in enterprises in Tashal during that time. This may have increased or sharply decreased his fortunes at the GMs discretion. Upon return to Gardiren, Akitt will be tried and hung the same day.

The manor originally had a wooden bridge leading to a gate. When the previous bailiff’s hunted out all the wolves in the local area, they filled in part of the moat and removed the gate and a portion of wall to ease access to the barn and manor house in anticipation of major construction work.

A pile of half-burned timbers and rubble mark the previous location of a small timber-frame building. It was the home of Akitt’s two mercenaries, Kenric and Hedin, until they left the fire unattended while drunk and it caught fire. After that, they lived in the main hall. The gatehouse was never rebuilt or even cleaned up.
The only things in this building are a single cart with a broken wheel and some rather motheaten tack. The thatched roof has come loose on the right rear corner and rain has leaked in.
This shelter once housed a dog-boy and several hunting dogs. Since the departure of Clan Morfan, it has stood empty. It is now home to a particularly territorial badger.

Until recently, this shed housed the four horses and three mules that belonging to Lord Akitt. It is in reasonable shape, though the floor has a thick layer of manure and is quite muddy. One poor stable boy lives in the loft. When Lord Akitt fired the ostler, he was left to tend all of the horses and mules, clean the tack and muck out the stables, an impossible task for a 13 year old boy. He was frequently beaten by the recently departed bailiff and cringes at the approach of any important looking person. He is starved for affection and will latch on to the first person who is nice to him.

Used as a granary, the barn is over thirty years old. Clan Morfan had planned to replace it in 716TR, but it was never done. The barn has a very distinct lean to one side as a result of weakening timbers. There is no foundation to speak of and the timbers were set directly in the ground causing them to rot badly. The barn is moderately full of goods that Akitt extorted from the villagers and didn’t have time to sell. With careful management, they might get the village through to the next harvest.

Built separately from the main hall in event of fire, this building is home to the two of the servants Akitt kept on after he assumed control of the fief. The cook is an older woman and was much abused by the men-at-arms. She is quite willing to tell everything she knows to anyone who will listen. The domestic is a young girl, once quite pretty; she cleaned, washed and served the lord and his men. In return for her hard work, she was raped regularly. She is now mute, though some tender loving care from another woman might get her to talk. After raping her, during what he felt was a sensitive moment, Akitt once told her his uncle lives near Thay.

This is a large timber-frame building on a stone foundation. It has a slate roof, which needs repairs in several locations and leaks badly over the front door when it rains. The solar and one-quarter of the main hall are paved with large flat flagstones, a project begun under the Clan Morfan. A stack of unused flagstones are piled outside the back of the hall where they have sat since 715TR. The room is dominated by a large central hearth; smoke filters out through a covered opening in the roof directly above the fire pit. The building has not been whitewashed in several years and some of the daub is beginning to flake off.

The solar was used by Lord Akitt and his guests. The two additional beds and crib date from the previous residents, probably the same time the sheets were last washed. There are outlines in the grime where three chests once stood.

When Sir Geleyn first became bailiff of Charmic Manor, there was quite a problem with wolves in the area. A large palisade, built of stout timbers and ten feet tall, was built to provide refuge for the villagers. After almost virtually eliminated the local wolf population, they replaced part of the wall with a low fence. Today fungus and rot have got into the wood and the whole thing could be knocked over with a stout kick.

Since the arrival of Lord Akitt, several rotten sections of the palisade have collapsed and nothing has been done to repair them. The wolf population has bounced back and now the population no longer has anywhere to seek refuge. Three villagers were killed last winter and the villagers now close up their homes the best they can and huddle together when the wolves are on the hunt.

The courtyard is a sea of mud and filth. Piles of rotting garbage and manure give it a disgusting reek. Large puddles of standing water mixed with animal urine dot the yard. The contents of the manor chamber pots have just been thrown in the corner of the palisade. The yard of the basest cottar is not this filthy.

Geographical Details

Charmic is a moderate sized fief in northern Kaldor, held as a personal fief by the Earl of Neph under a temporary bailiff, Sir Peart Tanush. The fief is only sixty-five years old, having been created by the previous Earl of Neph in 655TR as a new manor on which to settle a number of villeins from his other estates. Although located only five leagues south-east of Gardiren, Charmic is in a relatively isolated area, bounded on all sides by woods. The large Kirsta Forest to the south is a wild and forbidding place, full of wolves and brigands. The village sits next to a small stream which forms the boundary between Dobraine and Kirsta Hundreds. The manor is in a pleasant valley bottom with fine soil and moderate climate. All crops grow well and the estate has great potential.

The manor is at the end of the road from Gardiren. There is substantial traffic on the road up to the quarry a half a league away. From there, the road turns into a narrow, muddy track. Those unfamiliar with the route to Charmic Manor might well think the road is a dead end. The only other road from Charmic leads east to Zernhol Manor. The people of Zernhol prefer to take the road via Erwund Abbey to Gardiren. The Laranian abbey is rich and powerful and their road is well maintained and patrolled. The woods around Charmic have a bad reputation.

The bailiff owes the Earl £115 82d per year in feudal payments plus one Heavy Horse and four Light Foot. Due to the previous bailiff’s relationship to the Earl, the military obligation has been rendered as scutage (£7 48d per year). The manor has paid its full account of £122 130d each mid-summer’s day for the last five years.

History

Clan Morfan were made the Bailiffs of Charmic manor in 685TR. Originally a minor clan, their dedication and loyalty greatly impressed the Earl of Gardiren. Their leader, Sir Geleyn, was very devoted to his duties. He over saw the construction of a large and comfortable wooden manor house, a substantial palisade and several new buildings during his tenure as bailiff. With the Earl’s permission, he expanded the amount of cleared land and established over a dozen new households.

Sir Geleyn was well liked by the tenants. He was a fair and just lord. He worked tirelessly to improve the manor and expected the same of his tenants. He was responsible for recruiting a metalsmith and woodcrafter to compliment the miller.

An enthusiastic hunter, he and his three sons hunted out virtually all of the wolves and bears in the area, to the great relief of the peasants. His regular patrols discouraged bandits and brigands, while his efficient manor courts resolved most minor legal problems quickly and to the general satisfaction of the population.

From 685 to 715TR, the manor grew significantly. Sir Geleyn was prompt with his feudal obligations (both military and financial) and the Earl’s Steward was much impressed, resulting in a steady rise of the status of Clan Morfan within Earl Curo’s court during those thirty years. Therefore, few were surprised when the Earl granted Umbrea and Warial manors to Clan Morfan in 715TR. These two manors had reverted back to the Earl on the death of the last member of the Clan Thuen and their award to Clan Morfan was seen as a reflection of the Earl’s satisfaction with their loyal performance as Bailiffs and their worthiness to be permanent landholders.

During the summer of 715TR, Clan Morfan held a final manor court to say farewell to their tenants before leaving for Umbrea Manor. In addition to the departure of the family, they also took their men-at-arms and two yeomen families who followed them to their new holding.

The Bastard

The present Earl’s father was a man of lusty appetites, even in his later years. He fathered several bastards, including Akitt Llack. Akitt was acknowledged and lived with his mother in one of the Earl’s townhouses until the Earl died when he was twelve. His father’s widow hated him and ordered he and his mother immediately expelled from the only home he had ever known.

On the death of the Earl’s widow a decade later, Akitt was brought back to court. With his mother dead, Earl Curo wanted to ensure his half-brother was taken care of, be he baseborn or no. However, the life of the timbewright’s apprentice had ill-prepared Akitt for the life at court and he soon made a fool of himself.

Anxious to rid himself of an embarrassment, the Earl made Akitt bailiff of Charmic manor, a rich fief on the edge of his domain. Thinking he was being quite magnanimous, Curo sent Akitt off to the wilderness without recognizing the humiliation, rage and hate boiling in his veins.

The Dark Years

Akitt’s arrival in Charmic was unremarkable. He came with only a couple of men-at-arms (mercenaries) and his cousin Lynd (a timberwright). This was a far cry from the large household previously supported by the Clan Morfan.

Within a week, the peasants began to sense things were going to change. Almost immediately, Lynd began to explore the area, looking at stands of timber. When he began to blaze large oaks in the King’s forest (outside of the manor boundaries), the Woodward, Muir, became quite concerned and went to the new Bailiff. Far from supporting the Woodward’s concerns, Akitt became extremely angry and told Muir that if he ever questioned Lynd’s again, he would be beaten. The two mercenaries then threw Muir out of the hall.

The next rest day, Akitt summoned Witol the Reeve. He informed him that the King had granted him the right to as many oaks as he wished from unsettled land. He held up a writ with many seals and signatures in front of the illiterate man and told him that Lynd had already marked out the first trees to be cut.

For the rest of the summer and through the fall, the villagers cut trees. A new road was cleared, but the people were suspicious when they were ordered to only cut the largest trees, and never ones visible from the fields or road. The trees were felled and the logs transported to a new cutting yard, built in the middle of the village. The villagers spent many days cutting the logs into beams under the direction of Lynd, a ruthless task master.

So much logging was being done that normal fief maintenance suffered. Again, Witol approached Lord Akitt. He asked the bailiff to give him enough men to do normal repairs to the manor, roads and fences. He was flatly denied and was barely allowed enough men and time to bring in the harvest. Despite the lack of maintenance, Lord Akitt took every fee and tax he was due.

Wagons from the timberwright’s guild were regular visitors to the manor. The guildsmen were welcomed warmly by Lord Akitt and Lynd and many lavish feasts were held for them. Lord Akitt dismissed most of the staff who had worked for Sir Geleyn, but the few remaining servants reported that the guild master gave Lord Akitt many heavy pouches that he kept a large iron-bound chest in his room. The Bailiff kept the only key around his neck at all times.

Normally, winter is a time of rest for the peasants. The first winter under the new Bailiff was a rude change. Lynd drove the men mercilessly. Up before dawn for the long walk out to the logging area, the men worked right until last light before returning, exhausted, to their homes. The constant heavy labour left the men hungry. Under the rule of Clan Morfan, the men could have at least expected a good meal in the manor hall, but under Lord Akitt, they were left to live off of their own meagre stores of food. By spring, all of the households were hungry and short of food. Starvation was only averted by an early spring.

As expected, the winter took a toll on the manor. With the coming of spring, Witol the Reeve again approached the Lord with plans to repair the winter damage and catch up on the maintenance that had not been done the previous fall. This time, for questioning the Bailiff’s priorities, Witol was beaten by the men-at-arms for his insolence and driven from the hall. Immediately following the completion of spring planting and a bare minimum of other vital tasks, the men were again ordered to return to logging.

The pattern of ignoring fief maintenance and using every spare man to log the King’s forest continued for five years. In 717, Lord Akitt sacked the Reeve and replaced him with Jodoin, a cowardly yes-man who gladly enforced the Bailiff’s every command without question. Witol, who had so loyally served the Clan Morfan for thirty years, was stripped of his land when his son tried to run away. The boy was dragged back and cruelly beaten. He never recovered and died the following winter. Witol was reduced from villein to cottar and now struggles to feed his wife and remaining son.

Throughout this time, Akitt and his cousin got richer and richer, filling the first chest and adding two more. Each year, the tenants hoped and prayed that the Earl’s Steward come to Charmic and discover Lord Akitt’s cruel actions and remove him. He never arrived. Little did they know that the Bailiff faithfully paid the Earl exactly the same payments as Clan Morfan had for the last thirty years, and so the Steward saw no need to check up on the Earl’s own half-brother.

The harvest of 719TR was very bad. Despite this, Lord Akitt took his full share (most of which he sold at a handsome profit), leaving virtually nothing for the peasants. Faced with starving parishioners, Charmic’s Peonian priest could take no more and slipped away in the night to take word to the Earl. After walking all day, the priest arrived at the Earl’s castle in the middle of a feast. He convinced the guard to call the Steward out of the hall and informed him what was happening. When the Steward relayed the news to the Earl he summoned the village priest before him, questioning him in detail. Then, the Earl summoned the local Peonian priest from Gardiren to confirm the man was indeed from Charmic. Determined to convince the Earl, the village priest fell to his knees and swore a holy vow on the sacred relic of Peoni. Convinced by the man’s honesty, Earl Curo was furious and declared “the ungrateful wretch”, Akitt Llack, outlaw.

As he hurried through the town of Gardiren, the village priest was recognized by one of Akitt’s “business partners”, Naviel, who realized they would all hang when the Earl found out what was happening. Naviel rode to Charmic to warn Akitt while the Earl was busy interrogating the priest. In a flurry of activity, the bailiff, his halfbrother, two mercenary guards and Naviel rode out of Charmic in the middle of the night, only hours ahead of the Earl’s guards.

None of the five men have been seen since. Earl Curo has posted a large reward for the capture of these men so he can try them for corruption and theft. They also face Royal charges of theft, for cutting the King’s trees without leave.

Current Affairs

The corrupt bailiff, Akitt Llack, is gone. The Earl has sent a temporary bailiff, Sir Peart Tanush, and five men-at-arms to secure the manor and to salvage what can be salvaged. Sir Peart has temporarily relieved the tenants of all other duties but their work in the fields in hope of producing enough food so the villagers can survive the winter. He is taking stock of the manor house and other improvements on the fief. What he sees is not good. Once the harvest is secure, he will make what temporary repairs he can.

Sir Peart has made a preliminary report to the Earl. He has recommended that a new permanent bailiff be appointed as soon as possible. He recommended it be a man of action, as there is much work to be done. Currently secured by Sir Peart and his men, the village is safe, but the woods are filled with outlaws and wolves are roaming the manor by night. Several villagers have been attacked even within the limits of the village itself. The new bailiff will need to hunt down these wolves and put an end to the outlaws, not a task for a bureaucrat.

Whoever takes on the job will have a great deal of maintenance to catch up on and hostile villager’s to deal with. However, a skilful negotiator may be able to win concessions from the Earl, such as relief from feudal payments for a few years, to help pay for the repairs.

Sir Peart Tanush is the deputy to the Earl of Neph’s Steward. In this role, he is responsible for making assessments on manors for their feudal payments. A moderately skilled knight, he has a razor sharp mind and is extremely well educated. He is literate in three languages, a talented mathematician and has an excellent eye for value (especially the value of a manor, crops and livestock). This is his first visit to Charmic since Lord Akitt took over the manor from Clan Morfan. He is completely appalled. When he inspected the manor just before the previous bailiffs left it was in excellent shape and very capable of supporting a knight with a large household. He believes it will take at least three years to put things right. If PCs make friends with Sir Peart he can be a powerful ally in the Earl’s court, especially when the new bailiff has to negotiate future feudal payments.

Using the Scenes

A number of scenes are provided representing maps. These scenes depict both internal and external areas; internal areas are generally set at a 5-foot grid spacing, while exterior areas use much larger scaling. The following subsections describe some common elements of these scenes.

Map Notes

The scenes make extensive use of Map Notes to provide detailed description of important areas in the scenes. To view these map notes, click on the "bookmark icon" in the canvas toolbar. Map notes are not visible to players, only to the GM.

Text and Markings

In various areas text and or markings have been provided in the scenes to assist the GM. Generally this information is set to only be visible to the GM.

Stairs

Some stairs may have an arrow indicating the direction the stairs descend. When present these arrows are visible to all players.

Lighting

To control ambient lighting, use the "darkness" setting for the scene.

All scenes have been setup with Unrestricted Vision Range enabled, with a Vision Limitation Threshold set to 0.7. This allows all areas of the scene to be lit during the day, but vision is limited and lights are required at night.

Internal lamps and candle lights have been placed in indoor areas. These lights have been set to enable when the "darkness" setting is ≥ 0.2, that is, just after things start becoming dim.

Hârn has a cool climate, so all fireplaces and braziers are constantly lit.

Manor Servants

There are currently only three servants at the manor: the cook, one domestic (see @UUID[JournalEntry.64DcGjkkvPnWNGXf.JournalEntryPage.nsxlAA8kNWzcgcWY]{[M7] Kitchen}) and a stable boy (see @UUID[JournalEntry.64DcGjkkvPnWNGXf.JournalEntryPage.Gyj3Kcz99ikE7tqc]{[M5] Stables}). Clan Morfan supported twelve plus three men-at-arms. The previous chamberlain, Adilan of Morad, was a free man and was so disgusted by what he saw, he left Akitt’s service shortly after the bailiff arrived. He settled in Gardiren. He is well known to the people of Charmic and could do a great deal to help set things to right. The other domestics were fired by Lord Akitt for being too expensive. Most of them still live in the village. They would be more than happy to return to their old jobs, if they could be convince the new lord is better than the old one (not a difficult task, especially if the new bailiff hired Adilan as his chamberlain).

This building was used for the storage and maintenance of Lynd’s tools. Axes, saws, chisels and other tools are carefully stored on well built racks on the walls. The floor is packed earth, but is clean and recently swept. Good, dry scrap wood has been stacked in the corner to keep it out of the weather.

This fine, comfortable house was the home of Lynd, Lord Akitt’s cousin. He forced the woodcrafter and villagers to help him build it. It is the finest house on the manor. It is tended by Lynd’s former apprentice, Thales, a fine young lad from Gardiren. He was not involved in the pillaging of the manor and was equally badly treated by the two men. He is well liked by the villagers. After Akitt and Lynd fled, he remained and tidied up the house, expecting his master to return. Instead, Sir Peart Tanush, deputy Steward of Earl Curo, and five men-at-arms arrived. Appalled by the state of the manor house, he chose to set up residence here. The deputy Steward is currently taking stock of the manor. Impressed by the young apprentice, he has allowed him to stay on as a domestic until the fate of Charmic is decided.

This open faced shed is used to season the timber before sale. Most of the wood is in the form of large timbers cut from the heart of the tree. The rounded pieces left from this process are then cut into planks. Every few months, guildsmen would come and take stock of the available timbers and buy what they needed. Sir Peart has impounded this timber in the name of the King.

The large pit in the middle of the yard is used to cut logs into timbers. Trees are felled in the forest and any branches trimmed off for sale as wattle material or firewood. The logs are then hauled to the yard, where they are stockpiled before being cut into square or rectangular beams for use in timber-frame construction. The process of sawing the logs involves one man in the pit underneath the log hauling down on the saw, while the man on the top hauls the saw back up for the next cut. The man in the pit does most of the cutting action and eats a face full of sawdust. The man on top has to haul the heavy saw up with each stroke. Both are backbreaking jobs. Lynd forced the village men to take turns while he supervised. When they were to slow, he “encouraged” them with a long ox whip. Most of the men in the village and Lynd’s apprentice bear many scars from this whip.

Each day, the sawdust from the pit had to be dug out and piled into this bin. Lynd then sold the sawdust to tanners for the tannic acid. Nothing that could make him a profit was wasted. He even had a monopoly on firewood, forcing the villagers to buy the wood they themselves had felled, cut and piled.

Occupation: Bailiff and Master Timberwright

His blue eyes are a striking contrast to his jet black hair and make him stand out in a crowd. He is cocky and proud of his body, wearing tight leather pants and a leather jerkin which emphasize his physique. Lynd is a darling with the ladies. Although intelligent, he talks quite slowly, appearing to pause and carefully consider every word. Lynd is definitely more capable than his cousin, but fate granted the manor to Akitt. A broker for the timberwright’s guild, Naviel is a follower. Reasonably intelligent, he hates to make decisions and prefers to defer to others. He is of average size, with a slim build, green eyes and brown hair. He wears good clothes that always seem a little baggy on him as if they were hand-me-downs. Naviel has no tact and bluntly says whatever comes to mind. For the last five years, he has acted as Akitt’s agent, finding buyers for the timber and investing his profits. He has an extensive array of shady and illegal contacts throughout the kingdom. He keeps one penny in seven of Akitt’s ill-gotten gains.

Charmic village is a fair sized community. It has fortyone households consisting of 34 unfree serfs (13 villeins, 9 half-villeins, and 12 cottars), one free farmer, three guildsmen, two yeomen and one priest of Peoni.

The village grew up along the main road. The Peonian church was built later and now the village is expanding along the road to the mill. The square is the centre of the village and the two of the guildsmen have their homes opening onto it. The mill is a rare Kaldoric example of a wind powered mill. Wind power was chosen due to the unpredictable volume of water in the stream and the steady breeze that always flows down the valley. The manor house is built along the banks of the stream and a moat, now rather silted, encircles it.

The community consists of six main clans and a number of individual families. Lord Akitt used the clan ties to great effect, meting out punishments against the whole clan to force them to keep their own members in line. Few will runaway or rebel when their aunt or grandmother will be killed in retribution. Those without clan ties were even more vulnerable as they had no one to turn to for assistance or support. Most ended up becoming yes-men and lackeys for Lord Akitt out of shear survival. The three craftsmen (miller, metalsmith and woodcrafter) would normally have been safe from the worst excesses of the lord of the manor, but Akitt was ruthless to the point of demanding hostages every time they left the manor. He also sent one of his lackeys along with them to report their every move. Lord Akitt and his men kept a tight rein on everything that happened in the village, including killing one boy and taking the arm of his father for standing up to them.

Economics and Agrarian Life

Northern Kaldor has been settled since the days of the Kingdom of Serelind. However, this manor is relatively new and is still being developed. Charmic has 2060 gross acres, 432 wooded, leaving 1628 cleared acres. Of this, 799 acres support tenants and 829 acres are demesne. Prior to the arrival of Lord Akitt, this was an very productive fief, as it sits on rich alluvial topsoil.

The manor is extremely rundown. The peasants have been taxed and worked to the very limit. The manor buildings require a long list of repairs. The fief itself requires a lot of work. The roads are badly rutted and barely passable. The recent lack of maintenance and general neglect has greatly reduced its productivity. Under the rule of Clan Morfan, the manor had a fief index of 1.10. Under Lord Akitt, that value fell to 0.85, a sign of serious neglect.

The manor demesne used to support a large herd of cattle and sheep, but Lord Akitt sold them off as being too labour intensive. The cattle herd has dwindled to just twelve cows and one, rather old, bull. The sheep herd is also down, though the price of wool convinced Akitt to keep forty sheep and five rams. Starvation and high taxes have thinned the numbers of villager’s animals almost to nothing. A few pigs and one or two jealously protected goats are all that remain. The people of the village are generally thin and malnourished, with a few notable exceptions, mostly Akitt’s lackeys. The villagers are downtrodden and will not meet the eye of a noble or anyone else in authority.

A side effect of the starvation is fewer children or old people. Most of them died off during a series of hard winters with little or no food and the bad harvest in the fall of 719TR. The villagers hope that a new lord will find some way to get them through the winter, but it has been long since they had any hope. A new lord will have to work hard to earn their trust.

Girn is married. With only two acres, there is no way he can feed his wife and himself. In desperation, he has reluctantly become one of Akitt’s enforcers. Even selling himself, they have barely enough to eat. The couple’s home is little more than a cave built of rocks and thatch. The couple’s one son was taken by wolves in 719TR while checking on the family pig in a pen behind the house.

A member of the second largest clan, Eld is squeaking by through careful management of his twenty-two acres. Only his wife and his brother survived out of a family of seven. He lost his parents and two children to starvation in the winter of 717. Their deaths mean the survivors have enough to eat most days.
